title: High Molecular Weight DNA Extraction for Marine Macroalgal Tissue
author: Malia Moore
materials: To each pellet, add 10 mL G2 buffer, from the QIAGEN kit. Incubate at 50 °C for 30-60 minutes, or until the pellet is dissolved. Swirl the pellet to mix but do not try to pipette or vortex.
Equilibrate a QIAGEN Genomic-tip 100/G column with 4 mL of Buffer QBT.
Discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Flash‑freeze algal tissue
steps.instruction: Flash‑freeze at least 5 g wet algal tissue in liquid nitrogen.

steps.title: Prepare Carlson lysis buffer
steps.instruction: Prepare the desired volume of Carlson lysis buffer containing 100 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 9.5), 2 % CTAB, 1.4 M NaCl, 1 % PEG 8000, and 20 mM EDTA; stir overnight on a magnetic stirrer until homogeneous and free of precipitate.

steps.title: Lyophilize tissue
steps.instruction: Transfer the frozen tissue to a lyophilization container and freeze‑dry for 36–48 h.

steps.title: Macerate and dry again
steps.instruction: Macerate the lyophilized tissue with a clean spatula to increase surface area, then return to the lyophilizer for an additional 24 h.

steps.title: Store dried tissue
steps.instruction: Remove the dried tissue, place it with desiccant in a refrigerator for immediate use, or store at –80 °C for longer periods.

steps.title: Pre‑heat heat block
steps.instruction: Pre‑heat a heat block or water bath to 65 °C and position it inside a fume hood.

steps.title: Aliquot lysis buffer
steps.instruction: For each extraction, dispense 20 mL of Carlson lysis buffer into a 50‑mL Falcon tube.

steps.title: Add β‑mercaptoethanol
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, add 400 µL β‑mercaptoethanol (originally 50 µL) to the buffer, vortex to mix, and pre‑warm the solution to 65 °C for 30 seconds before proceeding.

steps.title: Grind tissue with PVPP
steps.instruction: Place 0.5 tsp (≈0.5 g) lyophilized tissue into a clean mortar, add 50–100 mg powdered PVPP, and grind with a pestle for ~30 seconds until a dry powder is obtained; avoid adding moisture and transfer immediately to the extraction tube.

steps.title: Combine tissue with warm buffer
steps.instruction: Add the ground tissue to the pre‑warmed lysis buffer and invert the tube 5 times to mix.

steps.title: Add first RNase A aliquot
steps.instruction: Add 40 µL RNase A to the tube and vortex for 5 seconds.

steps.title: Optional mixing on heat block
steps.instruction: If a heat block with mixing is available, set it to 65 °C and 300 rpm for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Incubate at 65 °C
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube at 65 °C for 1 hour. At the 30‑minute mark, add an additional 40 µL RNase A and invert 10 times to mix.

steps.title: Cool to room temperature
steps.instruction: Allow the tubes to cool to room temperature for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Extract with chloroform
steps.instruction: Add 20 mL chloroform, vortex in two 5‑second pulses, then centrifuge at 3 500 × g, 4 °C for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Collect aqueous phase
steps.instruction: In the fume hood, transfer the top lysate layer (≈14–18 mL) to a new 50‑mL Falcon tube using wide‑bore tips (≈1 mL at a time) without disturbing the interphase.

steps.title: Add potassium acetate
steps.instruction: Mix the lysate with 0.4 × volume of 5 M potassium acetate (KOAc) at room temperature, invert at least 10 times, then incubate on ice for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Second centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3 500 × g, 4 °C for 45 minutes.

steps.title: Recover supernatant
steps.instruction: Carefully pour off and retain the supernatant, leaving a small amount behind to avoid disturbing the polysaccharide‑salt pellet.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 0.7 × volume isopropanol, invert 10 times, and incubate at –80 °C for 15 minutes (do not exceed this time).

steps.title: Pellet DNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3 500 × g, 4 °C for 45 minutes (fixed‑angle rotors give a wall‑pellet with larger surface area).

steps.title: Remove supernatant
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant without disturbing the pellet; use sterile wipes to absorb liquid from the tube walls.

steps.title: Column binding
steps.instruction: Pass the DNA solution (in G2 buffer) through an equilibrated spin column by gravity flow.

steps.title: Wash column
steps.instruction: Wash the column with 8 mL Buffer QC, then repeat with another 8 mL Buffer QC.

steps.title: Elute DNA
steps.instruction: Place the column over a clean 50‑mL Falcon tube and elute with 5 mL Buffer QF pre‑warmed to 55 °C.

steps.title: Cool eluate
steps.instruction: Allow the eluate to reach room temperature.

steps.title: Isopropanol precipitation (second)
steps.instruction: Add 3.5 mL isopropanol to the eluate, invert 10 times, then incubate at –20 °C for at least 3 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Second DNA pellet
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 3 500 × g, 4 °C for 45 minutes.

steps.title: Ethanol wash
steps.instruction: Add 4 mL ice‑cold 70 % ethanol, invert 10 times, then centrifuge at 3 500 × g, 4 °C for 10 minutes (pellet location depends on rotor type).

steps.title: Final supernatant removal
steps.instruction: Discard the ethanol supernatant without disturbing the pellet; wipe tube walls with sterile wipes.

steps.title: Resuspend DNA
steps.instruction: Resuspend the DNA pellet in 100 µL TE buffer and incubate at room temperature, typically overnight.

steps.title: Transfer to LoBind tube
steps.instruction: Transfer the DNA solution to a nuclease‑free 1.5‑mL LoBind tube using a wide‑bore tip, store at 4 °C, and wait 48 hours before quantification on Nanodrop/Qubit for optimal relaxation.

steps.title: Optional size selection
steps.instruction: If a BluePippin is available, perform size selection to retain fragments >15 kb; expect a 50–70 % loss of DNA.
